title: Structured Cabling and Documentation
summary: Create a synthetic cable record that another learner can follow and check.
objectives: Record source, destination, port, and status accurately.
Explain why patch panels and labels support troubleshooting.
Recognize when physical work requires qualified supervision.

vocab.def: An organized panel where network cables are presented and connected for management.
A label that uniquely identifies a cable or connection record.
The two endpoints of a documented connection.

sections.heading: A record is a handoff
sections.body: A useful cabling record names both ends, the ports, rack locations, cable ID, and current status. It should be clear enough for another person to check without guessing.

sections.heading: Model before touching
sections.body: Use paper, diagrams, or approved classroom cables for practice. Physical work on live or installed infrastructure belongs to qualified supervision and an approved environment.

practice.prompt: Which record is most useful: 'blue cable in rack' or 'C-104, panel P2-18 to switch S1-18, active, checked 10:30'?
practice.answer: The second record is useful because it identifies the cable, endpoints, ports, status, and check time.

quiz.question: Why do consistent cable labels matter?
options: They make paths easier to verify and hand off
They allow work on live fiber without training
quiz.answer: They make paths easier to verify and hand off
